sources.title: Install on macOS | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: macOS 14+ supports Intel and Apple Silicon.

sources.title: Install on Linux | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Linux x86_64 and ARM64 packages are available.

sources.title: Mobile app | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: The iPhone TestFlight app continues chats, approvals, files, diffs and Git on an awake Mac; it lacks direct PR creation/merge controls.

sources.title: Providers and models | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Stable and experimental CLI adapters, per-route model/effort settings and Claude/Codex subscription or key profiles are documented.

sources.title: Non-Git projects | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Opt-in plain folders retain sessions without Git; branch-backed review requires Git.

sources.title: CLI automation | super.engineering Docs
sources.locator: CLI automation; Observe and steer; Durable teams
sources.finding: Bundled sc controls worktrees, reviews and app-managed sessions. Durable team runs have one to eight roles and require explicit reports.

sources.title: Orchestration overview | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: App-owned orchestration is available by default but requires explicit user invocation.

sources.title: Agent communication | super.engineering Docs
sources.locator: What the provider handles; Reuse sessions
sources.finding: Labeled roles send peer/group messages, interrupt, wait and read reports across providers.

sources.title: Coordination state | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Versioned shared state supports compare-and-set and advisory locks, without locking Git or files.

sources.title: Team workflows | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Parallel teams launch together; sequential workflows require explicit waits and later launches.

sources.title: Workspaces, projects, and worktrees | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Workspaces contain projects and worktrees; plain folders are separate and worktrees retain tabs/layout.

sources.title: Shared context | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Opt-in shared-context workspaces group repositories with common instructions and lazily created worktrees.

sources.title: Session history and restore | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: History retains worktree, surface and provider resume IDs; invalid provider bindings can fall back to fresh sessions.

sources.title: Notifications and approvals | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Running/Ready inbox, permission and input requests, completion/error notifications and keyboard queue navigation are documented.

sources.title: Review changes | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Anchored app-managed review threads have states and agent replies; findings can be routed to current, new or background chats.

sources.title: Git actions and pull requests | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Git/forge state selects commit, PR/MR, CI repair, review, merge or cleanup. Mechanical actions run directly while judgment actions use agents.

sources.title: Project config and scripts | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Setup, run and cleanup scripts use personal settings or versioned repository configuration.

sources.title: Remote workspaces (SSH) | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Opt-in SSH workspaces keep Git and provider processes on Linux/macOS hosts; host credentials and forwarding are required.

sources.title: Settings reference and privacy | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Local-first settings/history, optional experimental automations and a telemetry-off control are documented; update checks are independent.

sources.title: Files, mentions, and context | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Files and attachments are scoped to the active worktree; pasted context is explicit.

sources.title: Agent browser control | super.engineering Docs
sources.finding: Visible browser automation is opt-in; read and act commands have different grants.

sources.title: Docs | super.engineering
sources.finding: Native Rust UI uses Metal on macOS and Vulkan on Linux; embedded web previews remain separate.

sources.title: Terms of Service | super.engineering
sources.finding: The main app has a limited revocable license. Software is free; voluntary sponsorship unlocks no features.

sources.title: Privacy Policy | super.engineering
sources.finding: No desktop account is required. Provider requests go directly to providers; anonymous app telemetry can be disabled, while update checks remain separate.

sources.title: Super Engineering account-free local application
sources.locator: Desktop application; AI providers; local data; remote workspace docs
sources.finding: The desktop application requires no Super Engineering account. Project data and provider credentials are local, provider requests go directly to their providers, and optional SSH workspaces execute on user-controlled hosts. The core desktop ADE is user-operated, rather than merely a worker for a mandatory vendor control plane.
